..
Issued at 228 PM EDT Sun Aug 23 2026

Late morning GOES-East Day Cloud Phase RGB imagery and KMQT radar 
reflectivity show a few bands of isolated to scattered light rain 
showers this morning over mainly the central UP with bands of clouds 
across the rest of the UP. Temperatures at 850mb of around 5 C are 
above a Lake Superior that ranges from 12 C to 20 C, which ranges 
from "good enough for lake effect clouds" to "good enough for lake 
effect showers", reflecting the variable effects of lake effect that 
is ongoing this morning. Impacts will be low to none as the showers 
are not particularly intense, but it may keep temperatures from 
breaking out of the 60s today for all except for the south-central 
and Isle Royale which will see less clouds today. The brisk 
northwesterly flow today will continue, and the wind-driven waves of 
5-7 ft east of Marquette from 1-5 miles out from the shores will 
drive a high risk of dangerous swim conditions including rip 
currents.

RAP analysis shows a 1004mb low pressure over the Ontario/Quebec 
line with broad 1018-1020mb high pressure stretching from far 
northwestern Ontario to Missouri. The low is vertically stacked with 
deep 500mb troughing extending over much of eastern North America, 
opposed by a 500mb ridge spanning from the Four Corners region to 
the Canadian Prairie. While the trough will not be moving much 
tonight, the ridge axis will pivot from the Canadian Prairie
towards the Manitoba/Ontario line, which will advance the high 
pressure towards the UP and clear out skies for most after 00Z. 
As the high brings relaxing winds, efficient radiational cooling
will allow temperatures to plummet in the interior west 
tonight, with a few interior western locations reaching the mid 
30s (wouldn't be surprised if Alberta Ford Center or other 
traditional cold spots dipped to freezing). This will result in 
some patches of frost (especially on elevated surfaces or low 
spots where cold air pools), however, with the prior August heat
still hanging on in the soil temperatures, widespread frost is 
not forecast, so an advisory will not be sent this shift. 
However, some caution should still be taken for those in the 
interior west with sensitive vegetation. Also, with temperatures
falling overnight, a few patches of fog cannot be ruled out in 
areas sheltered from the wind in the west (around 20% chance).

As high pressure establishes itself over the region, dry weather and 
seasonable temperatures are expected Monday into Tuesday. Meanwhile, 
a 500mb trough currently over eastern Washington and southeast 
British Columbia will complete its journey around the northern 
periphery of the western CONUS ridge, arriving around the Northwest 
Angle Tuesday afternoon. This will drive significant PVA and also 
support a surface low of 1005-1010mb arriving near western Lake 
Superior by 00Z Wednesday. Moisture advects into the region ahead of 
the cold front and PWATs climb to 1-1.25 inches. Directional wind 
shear will certainly be present as southerly to southwesterly low 
level flow is contrasted with the westerly to northwesterly flow 
aloft, though speed shear is somewhat lacking as LREF 500mb winds by 
00Z Wednesday around the interior west are only around 25 kt. 
Instability is likely going to be sufficient for thunderstorms as 
Euro ensemble MUCAPE is 40-60% likely to exceed 750 J/kg for the far 
western UP by 00Z Wed. Instability probabilities fall off overnight, 
but by 18Z Wed, mean MUCAPE values for the east half are widespread 
over 1000 J/kg, though uncertainty in the available forcing by 
Wednesday afternoon to realize such an uncertain airmass (and paltry 
shear profiles to organize buoyant updrafts) casts doubt on the 
severe weather potential, though unorganized thunderstorms with 
plenty of available moisture can still bring notable rainfall, with 
the LREF probability of 0.5+ inches of rain by 06Z Thursday 
widespread 40-70%.

With 850mb temperatures around 60% likely to fall to around 8 C, 
some lingering light lake effect showers (or at least, cloud cover) 
is possible for Thursday into Friday. Models diverge on solutions 
beyond then as different members of different ensemble suites handle 
the persistent Four Corners ridge and troughs over Hudson Bay and 
southwestern Canada differently, but at least some period of ridging 
seems reasonable to bring dry weather to the UP to kick off the 
weekend before the next ridge-riding shortwave arrives.
